explanation: When `arr[mid] < target`, the recursive call passes `mid` as the new `low` instead of `mid + 1`. If the search narrows to a point where `low == high == mid` and `arr[mid] < target`, the recursive call `binary_search(arr, target, mid, high)` receives the exact same `low`, `high`, and therefore the exact same `mid` as the current call — the arguments never change, so the base case `low > high` is never reached and the recursion never terminates (it will run until it blows the call stack).
prompt: This recursive binary search has a bug. What's wrong?
choices: The recursive call for the 'search right half' branch passes `mid` instead of `mid + 1` as the new `low`, so when `low == high == mid` the arguments never change and the recursion never terminates
The base case should be `low >= high` instead of `low > high`, or the function will raise an IndexError on empty arrays
`mid` should be computed as `(low + high + 1) // 2` to avoid truncating toward the wrong half
The equality check `arr[mid] == target` should compare with `is` instead of `==` to correctly detect the target value
